summary.headline: Piccadily Agro Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.4% YoY to INR277.9 crore, with distillery revenue up 30.5% to INR271.3 crore; Q2 EBITDA margin 21.7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever second-quarter revenue, with standalone revenue from operations up 19.4% YoY to INR277.9 crore and H1 up 18.8% to INR548.4 crore. Branded alcobev (Indri, Camikara, Cashmir, Whistler) grew 38% in Q2 volume and 45% in H1 volume, with H1 branded revenue up 29% to INR175 crore. Bulk alcohol growth slowed sharply in Q2 (about 16% net of excise) as government ethanol orders were stayed by a Chennai High Court order until last week. Q2 EBITDA rose 9.5% to INR53 crore, with margin at 21.7%, and management cited raw material, transport and high-sea logistics cost pressure.

financial_highlights.change: +30.5% YoY from INR207.9 crore; 97%+ of revenue vs 89% last year

financial_highlights.value: INR92 crore net of excise (INR110 crore incl. excise)
financial_highlights.change: about +16% YoY net of excise; H1 net of excise INR174 crore vs INR135 crore, +29%

segments.name: Branded alcobev (Indri, Camikara, Cashmir, Whistler)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 38% YoY in Q2 and 45% in H1; H1 revenue INR175 crore, up 29%. Branded revenue grew from about INR10 crore (FY22 launch of Indri) to over INR500 crore in FY26. Management says branded is growing faster than bulk.

segments.name: Bulk alcohol / ethanol / IMIL
segments.commentary: Bulk alcohol revenue was INR92 crore net of excise in Q2, about 16% YoY growth, and INR174 crore in H1 (+29%). Management said bulk volumes were held back by a Chennai High Court stay on government ethanol orders, now released nationally.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh distillery
segments.commentary: Commissioned recently and in ramp-up; ethanol and IMIL sales have started and new FY27-28 ethanol orders are allocated. Management expects about 70% utilisation in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 growth to be much stronger than H1, with a marked difference in Q3 and Q4 numbers, and expects significant growth over FY26.
Management said it expects to achieve the distillery growth guidance of about 60-70% given earlier, but did not give a number for H2.
Indri volume guided to grow 20-22% YoY, reaching about 5 lakh cases in 3-4 years.
Utilisation guidance for H2 FY27: about 70% at Chhattisgarh and 70-75% at Indri ethanol capacity.
Company is working on a revised 3-year plan, to be given by year-end.
Sugar business demerger is in regulatory process; next milestone to be communicated through exchanges.
capex_capacity: Malt capacity is 30 KL per day; combined ENA ethanol capacity is 420 KLPD across Indri and Chhattisgarh.
Maturation inventory exceeded 96,000 barrels; the company aims to pass 100,000 barrels by end FY27, which it says would be the largest at any Indian distillery.
Chhattisgarh distillery: ethanol and IMIL sales commenced; utilisation is ramping up.
Indri ethanol tender allocation averages only about 33% to aggregators, which constrains utilisation.
Barrel cost about INR30,000-35,000 per barrel including duties; barrels are reused 2-3 times with cycles of 4-7 years.
demand_pricing: Management said demand picked up in early Q3 and expects it to continue into winter, when North India brown spirit demand peaks. Sales are heavily North India weighted.
Raw material pressure from poor weather (drought in South, corn and rice crop hit) is expected to ease after the December crop arrives, for 6-8 months.
NSR of INR9,274 per case in H1 is described as the highest in the Indian alcobev sector, but may vary with product mix.

International: UAE fell to about 10% of Indri's international sales due to geopolitical issues; US sales have not declined despite tariffs. Qatar and Oman were added in Q2 (33 countries, 43 duty-free locations).
Marketing spend is about 10% of sales for brands. Indri is claimed to hold about 40% of Indian single malt value share (internal estimate).

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing the bulk versus IMFL split, and what is the Q2 breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave Q2 bulk alcohol of INR110 crore incl. excise (INR92 crore net), up about 16% YoY net; H1 bulk net of excise rose 29% from INR135 crore to INR174 crore. It did not commit to continuing the disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did growth slow so sharply in Q2 versus H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited international volatility and the FTA-related pressure, which led to an industry recalibration. It said this has now settled.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60-70% distillery growth guidance still intact, and will branded grow at that pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branded has outgrown bulk in H1 and expects that to continue. Bulk was held back by the High Court stay, now lifted. It expects a stronger H2 and did not give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-4x growth in 3-4 years on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said alcobev revenue went from INR10 crore to over INR500 crore in four years, which it says exceeds the earlier projection.

qa_highlights.question: What is the barrel economics and cycle life?
qa_highlights.answer: A barrel costs about INR30,000-35,000 including duties before warehousing and liquid. Sweet wine barrels are used twice, bourbon barrels three times and wine barrels twice, with each cycle of 4-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ethanol utilisation at Indri and Chhattisgarh by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Chhattisgarh is expected to reach about 70% utilisation in H2, and Indri 70-75%, constrained by the ethanol tender allocation of about 33%.

risks_watch: Bulk alcohol volume and pricing depend on government ethanol allocation; the High Court stay was only recently lifted.
Raw material and logistics cost pressure, which has held back margin improvement.
Dependence on North India; the company did not provide a regional split.
UAE sales have fallen to about 10% of international sales; US tariffs are a headwind.
Q2 growth slowdown; whether H2 acceleration materialises.
Chhattisgarh ramp-up and the demerger of the sugar business are pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term branded and barrel strategy, but evasive on quantified H2 guidance and on the breakup of bulk versus branded data. Management attributed the Q2 slowdown to external factors and said pressures have settled.
key_quotes: We believe the forthcoming years offer significant opportunities to monetize this platform through rising utilization, sustained premiumization, product introductions, operating leverage and stronger cash generation.
We would like to mention this NSR is the highest in the country for any alcobev company, which is owing to our top-down approach.
Consequently, quarterly EBITDA margin will depend on the product mix as well as operating efficiency.
So we see a significant growth in terms of year-on-year basis.

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 19.4% YoY to INR277.9 crore, driven mainly by branded volume (+38% in Q2) and distillery volumes, with bulk growth held back to about 16% net of excise by a court stay that the brief says has now been lifted, so the H1 picture (+18.8%) is the better guide; the brief does not quantify any one-off gain or loss in the quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 21.7% with EBITDA up only 9.5% to INR53 crore, and management cited raw material, transport and high-sea logistics cost pressure, with relief only after the December crop for 6-8 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chhattisgarh distillery is commissioned and ramping, with ethanol and IMIL sales started and about 70% utilisation expected in H2 FY27; maturation stock is targeted above 100,000 barrels by end FY27, though that is storage, not productive capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 FY27 growth to be much stronger than H1, branded volumes grew 38% in Q2 and 45% in H1, and Indri volume is guided to grow 20-22% YoY, though no numeric H2 figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Indri ethanol utilisation is guided to only 70-75% with ethanol tender allocation averaging about 33%, and a revised 3-year plan is due by year-end, so a new capex could come with that plan, but no capex was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to quantify H2 growth and only reiterated the 60-70% distillery growth guidance, while H1 revenue grew 18.8% and Q2 bulk growth slowed to about 16% net of excise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 growth slowed sharply to 19.4% revenue and about 16% bulk growth, H2 acceleration is not quantified, and the 60-70% distillery growth guidance has no H2 number behind it, with the Chennai High Court stay only recently lifted.

rows.label: New FY27-28 ethanol orders allocated to Chhattisgarh
rows.why: New FY27-28 ethanol orders are allocated and bulk orders held back by the Chennai High Court stay are now released, supporting the stronger H2 that management expects.

rows.label: Qatar and Oman added to international markets
rows.why: Qatar and Oman were added in Q2, taking Indri to 33 countries and 43 duty-free locations, while UAE fell to about 10% of international sales.

rows.label: Sugar business demerger
rows.why: The demerger is in the regulatory process, with the next milestone to be communicated via exchanges, and no timing was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the branded and barrel strategy and the Chhattisgarh ramp, but evasive on quantified H2 guidance and bulk versus branded split, while analysts pushed on the Q2 slowdown and whether H2 acceleration materialises.
